text:
Lettuce.
DIFFICULTY
Fairly Easy
2/5
HARVEST SEASONS
Spring / Summer / Autumn

Quick-growing lettuce gives repeat leaves or hearts in cool, moist weather, spring–autumn. Slugs love young plants; heat/drought encourage bolting and tipburn. Sow hearting types in small batches to avoid a glut.

Quick facts
Germination

6–12 days

Sowing depth

Outdoors: 1/2 in.; trays: cover lightly.

Harvest

May – Oct

Yield (10 ft row)

10-20 heads

Ready in

From sowing: loose leaves 6–8 weeks; hearts 8–14 weeks

Sow

Mar–Aug in batches. Feb under cover. Sow suitable overwintering varieties Aug–early Sep.

Plant out

Mar–Aug. Protect early plants with fleece or cloches.

Row spacing

Outdoor seed rows: 12 in.; final spacing by type.

Plant spacing

Hearting: 12 in.; loose-leaf: 6 in. Check packet for compact types.

Recommended varieties
COS
Little Gem

Compact, crisp, sweet cos hearts for small gardens and repeat sowings.

LOOSE-LEAF
Salad Bowl

Loose leaves for small, repeated pickings without harvesting a whole head.

COS
Winter Density

Compact, cooler-season lettuce; use protection to extend salad harvests.

BUTTERHEAD
All The Year Round

Familiar butterhead for successive sowings; a soft-leaved alternative to cos and loose-leaf.

LOOSE-LEAF
Lollo Rossa

Frilled red loose-leaf for colour and texture. Pick outer leaves or take whole young plants.

Key risks
Slugs

Ragged leaves and slime trails are signs of slugs.

Root aphid

Plants may suddenly wilt and die as soil-dwelling aphids attack roots.

Bolting

Lettuces produce thick flowering stems if left in the soil after hearts have formed.

Downy mildew

Older leaves, especially in damp autumn weather, may develop mildew.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
64
SALADS & LEAVES

Cool, moist soil gives tender leaves.

Sun or light shade is suitable; hot, dry conditions encourage bolting.

Prepare a clean, fertile bed.

Well-rotted compost helps the soil hold water evenly.

Water deeply.

Give hearting lettuces a good soak when the soil dries out.

Soil & preparation
Cool, moist, humus-rich, drained soil. Clear the bed; add rotted compost or manure.
Add compost regularly to heavy clay. Allow room under fleece/cloches for early growth.
Sowing & planting
Sow little and often
Thin for the type
Sow 

Space seed thinly in shallow drills. For early crops or beds troubled by slugs, use modules and barely cover the seed. Keep trays cool and shaded in heat.

Plant out 

Water the holes first. Just cover the roots, keep the lower leaves clear of the soil and firm gently.

Looking after the crop
Thin to the spacing for hearting or loose-leaf crops. Compact varieties may stand closer.
Keep beds clean and weed-free, with bare soil between plants to reduce slug shelter.
Water deeply when needed, especially hearting crops, to encourage deep roots. Daily light sprinkling favours slugs and shallow rooting.
Protect early plants with fleece or cloches for faster growth. Established young plants tolerate light frost.
Harvesting & storage
Pick larger outer leaves. Leave the centre and at least four young leaves to grow on.
Cut or pull hearts as soon as they feel firm: peak quality soon gives way to bolting, especially in warmth.
Cut close to use; trim roots/damaged leaves. Young, steady-grown plants taste best. Compost old plants before slugs or seeding; some cut hearts regrow small shoots for an extra picking.
Pests & diseases
Problem	What to look for	What to do
Slugs	Ragged leaves; slime trails.	Hand-pick after dark; protect seedlings.
Root aphid	Wilting; white patches on roots.	Water well; choose root-aphid resistance.
Bolting	Flower stems; bitter leaves.	Water steadily; sow in season; pick promptly.
Downy mildew	Yellow patches; white mould beneath.	Remove affected leaves; space and ventilate plants.
Aphid	Sticky, curled leaves; colonies.	Squash colonies; encourage predators.
Grey mould (Botrytis)	Grey mould; rotting stems.	Remove diseased plants; clear debris; ventilate.
Cutworm	Stems severed at soil level.	Search beside cut stems; remove caterpillars.
Tipburn	Brown, scorched leaf edges.	Keep moisture steady; remove decaying leaves.
No hearts	Hearting varieties stay open.	Check variety and maturity; space and water well.
Final tips

Keep summer seed trays cool and shaded.

Pick outer leaves without damaging the growing point.

Sow hearting lettuces in succession to avoid a glut.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
